description: Taxes on the developer’s sales to users, with Stripe Tax on their own payout account (they are the seller; the taxes are theirs, Neblla only sets it up for them). "status": settings status (active/pending, and what is missing), head office, defaults and active registrations. "set_head_office": the business address ({ country, postal_code, city, line1, state? }). "set_defaults": the default product tax code (txcd_…, e.g. txcd_10000000 for general digital goods — check with the developer) and tax behaviour. "add_registration" / "expire_registration": the jurisdictions where the developer is registered to collect tax ({ country, type, state? } — type as Stripe names it, e.g. "standard", "oss_union", "state_sales_tax"); with no registration in the buyer’s location no tax is collected. "report": itemized tax transactions — call with { from, to } to start it, then with { runId } until it returns a download link. "app": switch automatic tax on or off for one app’s checkouts ({ appId, automatic, inclusive? }); it only applies while the settings are active. By default the price INCLUDES the tax (what a European consumer expects); { inclusive: false } adds it on top (usual for businesses or the US). Neblla’s 1 % stays on the pre-tax amount either way. Registering with a tax authority is the developer’s legal step — never add a registration they have not confirmed. The same settings and the tax reports are also in the developer’s own Stripe Dashboard (Tax).

from.description: ISO date, start of the report interval

inclusive.description: app: the tax is included in the price (default true) or added on top (false)

to.description: ISO date, end of the report interval (exclusive)

name: neblla_tax
